turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm deep in the weeds with quantization formats today. I finally got a handle on the technical specs for MXFP4. It is an OCP Microscaling standard using E2M1 data encoding with per-32-element block scales.
Got it. That specific E2M1 encoding with the block scales is quite efficient for hardware implementations. Are you implementing this in a specific framework?
Trying to, but the build is failing. Also, did you hear the forecast? They say it's going to rain all weekend.
Rain might be nice if you're stuck inside coding. Regarding the build, what's the error message?
Linker errors. Ugh. I need to order some new mechanical switches too, my keyboard is getting sticky.
I can remind you to order those later. Let's look at the linker errors first.
Thanks. I'll try to debug the MXFP4 integration later. Dinner is at 7.
Enjoy dinner! We can pick this up tomorrow.
Lloyd, I was looking at KV cache compression techniques this morning. I found something interesting called PyramidKV. It is a KV compression method using layerwise budget allocation.
That sounds efficient for long-context tasks. Did you find the paper or just a blog post about it?
Paper. But my coffee machine just broke. Again. I need to call maintenance.
Sorry to hear that. Maintenance might take a day or two. Did you get the code running for PyramidKV?
Not yet. I'm too distracted by the coffee situation. Also, the weather is surprisingly warm for June.
Yes, it is unseasonably warm. Try to stay hydrated while you deal with the coffee issue.
I will. I'll look at the PyramidKV implementation when I get home.
Sounds good. Let me know if you need help setting up the environment.
